summary: Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale University, and Yale Divinity School. He held posts at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean of the College (1977–1982).

Jong-Nam Choi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the International Buddhist University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1994) under Yasunori Ejima and others, later serving as a researcher at the University of Mysore (1992) and associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA 1994) under Robert Buswell, he served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University, where he later held various academic positions from 1950 and became professor emeritus (1970–1989), alongside leadership roles at Soai Gakuen and other institutes.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink, later serving as an NWO research fellow (1989–1993) and associate professor at Leiden University from 1993.

Josef Horovitz was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies. He completed his doctorate under Eduard Sachau (~1893–1898) and held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1914–1931).

Josef Schick was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen and the University of Berlin (PhD 1887–1889). He held academic posts at the universities of Berlin, Bonn, and Heidelberg, before serving as ordinary professor at Munich (1896–1925).

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian who studied at the University of Munich (~1882–1885). He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (~1925–1937).
Josef van Ess was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1953–1959). He subsequently held a long-standing academic post at the University of Tübingen (~1968–1999).

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar who studied at Dartmouth, Columbia University, the University of Paris, and the University of Munich. After teaching briefly at Canterbury School, he taught at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).
Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). He served at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and later was Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (1847–1885).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College, the University of Maryland, Sorbonne, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1960), and was a longtime professor of geography at the University of Minnesota (1964–2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at University College School and the University of London, he served as a scholar and President at Harris Manchester College, Oxford, and at the University of Oxford.

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied at Columbia University and under traditional masters including Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist and scholar of Buddhist and Central Asian studies. Educated at Sciences Po, EPHE, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, he directed the Musée Guimet, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and DAFA.

Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University (PhD ~1932), and Union Theological Seminary, holding posts at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Loizzo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. Educated at Amherst College and Harvard University, he studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science, and was a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Joseph M. Kitagawa was a religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Rikkyo, CDSP, Seabury-Western, and the University of Chicago under Joachim Wach, he taught at Chicago from 1951, serving as Dean of the Divinity School.
